# First literal GIC step and the remaining R2 interface

The proposed first check is `ValidatorNativeGic254.lean` with eight probes
and ten typed clients. It is source-only. The guard is unexecuted. It imports
only the already checked `ValidatorQuantifierCore254`; its precise boundary
is 21 project pairs, three direct external pairs plus the inherited Seq
anchor, and Init/Omega. No new Foundation cache build is required.

The new statement is uniform in every arithmetic value of an IΣ₁ model,
including nonstandard values and zero. It projects the container and GIC
halves of the literal bundle. The explicit `internalGic a b c p` records the
fact that the bundle uses its third argument as both the matrix code and a
variable label. The theorem supplies `internalGic a b (pad p) (pad p)` when
`a,b ≤ 3`, where `pad p = wim (wim p 1) 1`. Double-negation introduction and
elimination establish CProv equivalence of `p` and `pad p`; the arithmetic
constructor bound proves `pad p > 3`, discharging both bundle gates. This
works at `p=0`, unlike the ordinary `((p→p)→p)` padding argument whose numeric
size proof assumes a positive encoded formula. The final displayed theorem
generalizes the domain label 3. It leaves other parameters open.

This is an actual literal axiom introduction, not yet an encoding theorem
for `NativeGicDelta1.gicBodyVal`. In particular, numeric distinctness of the
three labels alone does not establish absence of capture inside the matrix.

## Exact next target

For arbitrary internally typed binary code
`K : Bootstrapping.Semiformula V ℒₛₑₜ 2`, prove

```text
CProv (ValidatorEnvironmentLabels254.encode F 0 s (gicBody K).val).
```

The theorem must state concrete freshness/environment conditions, or choose
a definable adequate environment and stream. A useful matrix encoding is
`P := encode F (2 ∷ 3 ∷ 0) t K.val`: input label 2, output/domain label 3,
and free parameters in odd labels outside 3. The existing fallback free label
is 1, so it is separate from these two input labels. The literal theorem above
already permits labels 2 and 3 through `cProv_paddedGic_bounded`.

One promising capture proof uses parity. `pad P` is divisible by four.
Choose an odd binder stream `t+2*k`, odd free labels, and avoid label 3 in the
free environment. Then `pad P` differs from every free/allocated binder
label; its `>3` bound also separates it from input labels 2 and 3 and the
fallback 1. The existing `encode_vac` can turn these explicit conditions
into the required CProv vacuity. This is a proposal, not a proved parity or
capture lemma in this packet. It avoids choosing a fresh stream after seeing
its own encoded output, which would be circular.

The first substantive bridge should identify the two substituted occurrences
of `K` in `gicBodyVal` with the same matrix encoding under the support and
coverage bound stacks, allowing the required swaps. Current
`ValidatorEnvironmentInstantiation254.encode_substs1` handles a single
free-variable substitution; it does not yet prove this simultaneous
two-variable permutation. Generalizing its `Ext` proof to a two-slot bound
environment relation is a direct source-syntax task. Then use the checked
finite quantifier/implication/conjunction congruence laws and paired-environment
alpha transport to compare the literal GIC instance with the Foundation
body. Do not rewrite a bundle row under an arbitrary variable renaming: that
would change the third argument's matrix-code role.

## Closure, axioms, and derivations are separate

`NativeGicDelta1` now has a root-owned actual PASS at
`/tmp/zfc-native-gic-delta1-check/run1/verification.json`, SHA
`e34df99cfd7e421ead95cf25329f59b41237d66aaf4ab885f582e7a3f5cf27ca`.
It proves the body/quotation graphs and GicR recognizer in arbitrary IΣ₁
models. It does not itself translate recognized native axioms into CProv.
`NTemplate.nativeGicProof` proves an internal GIC theorem *in nativeTheory*,
not a validator theorem. Its all-internal recognition proof can inform the
membership split, but cannot replace the target axiom-introduction proof.

After the body bridge, arbitrary `GicR p` must be decomposed through
`SchemaRecognizer`: internal closure count, closed source body, and an
internal binary core. The validator side then needs internal-many successive
generalizations plus the exact closed-body encoding identity. This requires
induction over the internal count, not a standard Lean list of quantifiers.
For nativeTheory, also prove the equality and fixed container/irreflexivity
branches at internal codes, then translate arbitrary internal derivations,
including opening, EXS instantiation, logical rules and their side conditions.
The endpoint is `Provable nativeTheory ⊥ → CProv 1`; no part of this packet
asserts that endpoint or uses ordinary completeness on nonstandard formulas.

The existing environment proof transport is not uniformly IΣ₁-strength:
`ValidatorEnvironmentVacuity254.encode_vac`,
`ValidatorEnvironmentAlpha254.encode_eq_under`, and
`ValidatorEnvironmentStreams254.encode_formula_relabel` explicitly require
IΣ₂ because their induction invariant is Π₂. The current concrete route can
therefore target PA, or explicitly IΣ₂. An IΣ₁ R2 theorem still needs a lower
complexity proof-witness construction. The syntax-only instantiation theorem
does remain IΣ₁.

## Root execution proposal

After source and guard review, root may run the following sequentially with
fresh external output directories. No command has been executed by this lane.

```sh
python3 -B /tmp/zfc-validator-native-gic/check.py --prepare-only --output /tmp/zfc-validator-native-gic/prepared1
python3 -B /tmp/zfc-validator-native-gic/check.py --output /tmp/zfc-validator-native-gic/run1
```

The new guard preserves the reviewed NativeGic runner's shared 120-second
source/audit deadline, one compiler thread, 4096 MiB and default proof
options, with explicit target-directory creation. The parent is the actual
QuantifierCore 25/18 PASS, whose older record contains
`fresh_object_sha256_before_audit` but no modern first-provider capture. The
guard checks that historical hash and current first-provider search order;
it does not invent a stronger historical capture. External Foundation/Mathlib
transitive object caches remain supplied boundaries, with exact selected
source/object pins and dependency revisions.

import ZFCinPA.ValidatorQuantifierCore254

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

/-!
Literal all-internal GIC introduction for the validator. The bundle's third
argument serves both as its matrix code and as an existential variable label.
Double-negation padding supplies the two numeric gates at labels 1 and 3,
including when the input matrix value is zero. This unit does not identify
the result with the configurable encoding of a Foundation GIC body: capture
avoidance, alpha transport, universal closure and the proof translation remain
separate obligations.
-/
namespace LeanProofs.ZFCinPA.ValidatorNativeGic254
open LO LO.FirstOrder LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic
open _root_.SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC
open ArithmeticCantor ArithmeticCode254
open ValidatorProvability254 ValidatorQuantifierCore254
open scoped LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic

variable {V : Type*} [ORingStructure V] [V↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧* 𝗜𝚺₁]

/-- Domain occupies label b; the collection witness uses c. The matrix p is
evaluated under the two input labels a and b in the literal G circuit. -/
noncomputable def internalGic (a b c p : V) : V :=
  ex c (conj
    (wal a (wim (wel a b) (wal b (wim p (ex b (conj p (wel b c)))))))
    (wal b (wim (wel b c) (ex a p))))

lemma bundleG_eq_internalGic (a b c : V) :
    ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c = internalGic a b c c := rfl

private lemma cProv_native_pair (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (conj (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c)
      (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c)) := by
  have hall : CProv (conj
      (conj (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c) (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c))
      (conj (wim (wel a b) (wal c (wel a b))) (wim (weq a b) (wal c (weq a b))))) := by
    change CProv (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundle a b c)
    exact cProv_bundle a b c hca hcb
  exact cProv_mp (conj_left _ _) hall

lemma cProv_container (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c) := by
  exact cProv_mp (conj_left _ _) (cProv_native_pair a b c hca hcb)

lemma cProv_internalGic (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (internalGic a b c c) := by
  exact cProv_mp (conj_right _ _) (cProv_native_pair a b c hca hcb)

/-- This padding preserves the matrix up to actual CProv equivalence and
forces a code above 3 without a nonzero-matrix premise. -/
noncomputable def pad (p : V) : V := wim (wim p 1) 1

lemma pad_gt_three (p : V) : (3 : V) < pad p := by
  have hc : (1 : V) ≤ cantor (wim p 1) 1 := (components_le _ _).2
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hc (show (0 : V) ≤ 4 by simp)
  have hp : (4 : V) ≤ pad p := by
    simpa only [pad, wim, tagged, add_zero, mul_one] using hm
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (show (3 : V) < 4 by simp) hp

lemma pad_equivalent (p : V) :
    CProv (wim p (pad p)) ∧ CProv (wim (pad p) p) :=
  ⟨double_neg_intro p, double_neg_elim p⟩

lemma cProv_paddedGic_bounded (a b p : V) (ha : a ≤ 3) (hb : b ≤ 3) :
    CProv (internalGic a b (pad p) (pad p)) :=
  cProv_internalGic a b (pad p)
    (ne_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_lt ha (pad_gt_three p)))
    (ne_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_lt hb (pad_gt_three p)))

theorem cProv_paddedGic (p : V) :
    CProv (internalGic 1 3 (pad p) (pad p)) :=
  cProv_paddedGic_bounded 1 3 p (by simp) (le_refl 3)

/-- Close the domain label of the literal G instance. Other parameter labels
are still free: this is not the arbitrary universal closure recognizer. -/
theorem cProv_closed_paddedGic (p : V) :
    CProv (wal 3 (internalGic 1 3 (pad p) (pad p))) :=
  cProv_gen 3 (cProv_paddedGic p)

end LeanProofs.ZFCinPA.ValidatorNativeGic254

/-!
Literal all-internal GIC introduction for the validator. The bundle's third
argument serves both as its matrix code and as an existential variable label.
Double-negation padding supplies the two numeric gates at labels 1 and 3,
including when the input matrix value is zero. This unit does not identify
the result with the configurable encoding of a Foundation GIC body: capture
avoidance, alpha transport, universal closure and the proof translation remain
separate obligations.
-/
namespace LeanProofs.ZFCinPA.ValidatorNativeGic254
open LO LO.FirstOrder LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic
open _root_.SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC
open ArithmeticCantor ArithmeticCode254
open ValidatorProvability254 ValidatorQuantifierCore254
open scoped LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic

variable {V : Type*} [ORingStructure V] [V↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧* 𝗜𝚺₁]

/-- Domain occupies label b; the collection witness uses c. The matrix p is
evaluated under the two input labels a and b in the literal G circuit. -/
noncomputable def internalGic (a b c p : V) : V :=
  ex c (conj
    (wal a (wim (wel a b) (wal b (wim p (ex b (conj p (wel b c)))))))
    (wal b (wim (wel b c) (ex a p))))

lemma bundleG_eq_internalGic (a b c : V) :
    ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c = internalGic a b c c := rfl

private lemma cProv_native_pair (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (conj (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c)
      (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c)) := by
  have hall : CProv (conj
      (conj (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c) (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleG a b c))
      (conj (wim (wel a b) (wal c (wel a b))) (wim (weq a b) (wal c (weq a b))))) := by
    change CProv (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundle a b c)
    exact cProv_bundle a b c hca hcb
  exact cProv_mp (conj_left _ _) hall

lemma cProv_container (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (ArithmeticTemplates254.bundleC a b c) := by
  exact cProv_mp (conj_left _ _) (cProv_native_pair a b c hca hcb)

lemma cProv_internalGic (a b c : V) (hca : c ≠ a) (hcb : c ≠ b) :
    CProv (internalGic a b c c) := by
  exact cProv_mp (conj_right _ _) (cProv_native_pair a b c hca hcb)

/-- This padding preserves the matrix up to actual CProv equivalence and
forces a code above 3 without a nonzero-matrix premise. -/
noncomputable def pad (p : V) : V := wim (wim p 1) 1

lemma pad_gt_three (p : V) : (3 : V) < pad p := by
  have hc : (1 : V) ≤ cantor (wim p 1) 1 := (components_le _ _).2
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hc (show (0 : V) ≤ 4 by simp)
  have hp : (4 : V) ≤ pad p := by
    simpa only [pad, wim, tagged, add_zero, mul_one] using hm
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (by simpa only [three_add_one_eq_four] using (lt_add_one (3 : V))) hp

lemma pad_equivalent (p : V) :
    CProv (wim p (pad p)) ∧ CProv (wim (pad p) p) :=
  ⟨double_neg_intro p, double_neg_elim p⟩

lemma cProv_paddedGic_bounded (a b p : V) (ha : a ≤ 3) (hb : b ≤ 3) :
    CProv (internalGic a b (pad p) (pad p)) :=
  cProv_internalGic a b (pad p)
    (ne_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_lt ha (pad_gt_three p)))
    (ne_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_lt hb (pad_gt_three p)))

theorem cProv_paddedGic (p : V) :
    CProv (internalGic 1 3 (pad p) (pad p)) :=
  cProv_paddedGic_bounded 1 3 p (by simp) (le_refl 3)

/-- Close the domain label of the literal G instance. Other parameter labels
are still free: this is not the arbitrary universal closure recognizer. -/
theorem cProv_closed_paddedGic (p : V) :
    CProv (wal 3 (internalGic 1 3 (pad p) (pad p))) :=
  cProv_gen 3 (cProv_paddedGic p)

end LeanProofs.ZFCinPA.ValidatorNativeGic254

# Literal internal GIC introduction

[ValidatorNativeGic254](Lean/ZFCinPA/ValidatorNativeGic254.lean) and its
[typed audit](validator_native_gic254_audit.lean) passed a fresh Lean source/audit
check: **8 named probes, 10 typed callers, zero warnings**. The selected run
used 2.509 seconds for the source and 2.025 seconds for the audit. The
[actual record](results/validator-native-gic254-verification.json) and
[author-disclosed evidence review](results/validator-native-gic254-review.json)
retain the exact source, snapshots, provider identities and pre-audit object.

For every ordered-ring model of IΣ₁ and every internal matrix value `p`, the
unit extracts the literal C/G formulas from the checked validator bundle.
It defines `pad p := ¬¬p`, proves actual `CProv` implications both ways and
proves `pad p > 3`. This supplies the bundle's numeric side conditions at
labels 1 and 3, even for `p = 0`, and gives a `CProv` proof of the literal G
instance with both matrix and witness label `pad p`. A final theorem closes
the domain label 3. It does not close every free parameter.

This is a literal validator formula theorem. Identifying it with the
configurable encoding of an arbitrary internal Foundation GIC matrix still
requires simultaneous substitution, capture avoidance and alpha transport.
General universal closure, all native-axiom cases and the internal derivation
translation to `CProv 1` remain separate. The unit establishes no new machine
state bound or internal PA consistency endpoint.

The first actual source attempt failed at the numeric proof of `3 < 4`:
`simp` made no progress. It produced no successful module or audit run.
The successor changes only that proof term to use `lt_add_one` and
`three_add_one_eq_four`. The statements and audit are identical; the renamed
boundary is byte-identical, and the guard changes only the selected source
hash and the source/boundary paths. [Exact history](results/validator-native-gic254-history.json)
preserves both preparations, the failed and successful raw records/logs,
original and successor sources/guards, snapshots, numeric repair and reviews.

Each source/audit attempt shares 120 seconds, with `-j1 -M4096` and default
proof limits. The successful audit reports only `propext`, `Classical.choice`
and `Quot.sound`. The guard records the fresh object and its first-provider
identity before audit and rechecks all inputs afterwards. It performs no
compiler-version query, dependency build or download.

The exact [QuantifierCore parent](validator_quantifier_core254.md) supplies
21 selected project source/object pairs including its fresh module. Three
direct external import pairs, the inherited Seq pair, and Init/Omega remain
pinned. The 74 current inputs were checked in the evidence review. The
historical parent provides its own pre-audit object hash but lacks the newer
first-provider capture; that limitation is preserved. The external caches
are supplied boundaries and are not wholly re-attested. Exact historical
cached inputs remain prerequisites; no compiled objects are distributed and
this is not a clean-checkout rebuild procedure.

The installed guard changes four path defaults only. From this directory,
with the recorded inputs available:

```sh

python3 -B check_validator_native_gic254.py --output /tmp/validator-native-gic254-actual
```
